question.text: The Negotiated Dealing System - Order Matching (NDS-OM) is an anonymous, electronic, screen-based, order-driven platform for trading in government securities. It is owned by __________ and managed by __________.

answer.text: RBI; Clearing Corporation of India Ltd (CCIL)

explanation.text: The Logic: NDS-OM is the primary electronic platform for trading government securities in India. It is owned by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and managed and operated by the Clearing Corporation of India Ltd (CCIL). The platform is anonymous, screen-based, and order-driven, used primarily by institutional participants such as banks, primary dealers, insurance companies, and mutual funds. RBI has also recently permitted SEBI-registered stock brokers to access NDS-OM through a Separate Business Unit (SBU) for facilitating retail investor trades. The Trap: Students may assume SEBI regulates G-Sec trading platforms since SEBI is the securities market regulator. The government securities market is regulated by RBI, not SEBI; NSE and NSDL are SEBI-regulated entities and do not manage NDS-OM. Note: Pair them as RBI-owned and CCIL-managed, and remember that access is not strictly limited to institutions — SEBI-registered brokers can route retail trades via an SBU.
